title: Grandfathered-Rule Migration for Pre-ADR-072 Cycles
summary: The Stop hook detects pre-ADR-078 `cycle-status.md` files (single-entry, no `## Cycle Stack` header) and, within them, pre-ADR-072 entries lacking cycle-shape fields, and applies grandfathered enforcement: advisory-mode manifest checks regardless of the corpus-level `.migration-version` state, until the user runs a new `/rdd-conform` cycle-shape audit scope, manually adds current-schema fields, or graduates the cycle (ADR-025). The audit detects legacy entries, reads and prompts for missing fields, and writes a migrated entry into the current stack format while preserving the existing prose body verbatim. Cycle 8 (rdd-pair) is named as the validation case.
workflow_point: Stop hook cycle-status.md legacy detection; /rdd-conform cycle-shape audit scope
mechanism: grandfathered advisory-mode enforcement for pre-ADR-072 cycles, migrated via a /rdd-conform audit scope

links.note: graduating a grandfathered cycle (ADR-025) closes it and ends the grandfathered window with it
handles the per-cycle migration transition on top of ADR-070's corpus-level enforcement-mode/advisory-mode boundary (the .rdd/.migration-version file)
grandfathers cycles that predate ADR-072's cycle-shape fields (Skipped phases, Paused, Cycle type) into advisory-mode enforcement until migrated
detects pre-ADR-078 cycle-status.md files (single-entry, no Cycle Stack header) via ADR-078's legacy single-entry-format treatment, then migrates them to the current stack schema
ADR-080's precondition framework provides the mechanism by which grandfathered checks are skipped, though the detection of legacy format is hook logic rather than a precondition itself
